readers.summary: react-native-vision-camera 5.2.3 (verified in C:\dk\mobile\node_modules\react-native-vision-camera\src) is a Nitro rewrite: there is NO `format`/`photo={true}`/`camera.current.takePhoto()` API any more. You render `<Camera device={...} isActive={...} outputs={[photoOutput]} style=... />`, where `photoOutput = usePhotoOutput({...})` is a `CameraPhotoOutput` HybridObject, and you capture with `photoOutput.capturePhoto(settings, callbacks): Promise<Photo>` (in-memory) or `photoOutput.capturePhotoToFile(settings, callbacks): Promise<{filePath}>`. Permission is `useCameraPermission()` (or `VisionCamera.cameraPermissionStatus` / `VisionCamera.requestCameraPermission()`); the back device is `useCameraDevice('back')`, or simply pass the string `device="back"`. Recommended still-capture flow for the classifier: `capturePhoto` -> `photo.saveToTemporaryFileAsync()` (plain filesystem path; prepend `file://` for RN `<Image>`/upload) AND `photo.toImageAsync()` (a react-native-nitro-image `Image` with rotation/mirroring physically applied) -> `cropAsync` center square -> `resizeAsync(224,224)` -> `toRawPixelDataAsync()` (RGBA on Android, 4 bytes/px) -> strip alpha in JS -> `photo.dispose()` + dispose Images. No Expo config plugin exists in the package (no app.plugin.js) and the library manifest declares only `uses-feature`, but C:\dk\mobile\app.json already lists `android.permission.CAMERA` and the generated AndroidManifest already contains it. Nothing in this flow touches worklets/frame processors: `react-native-vision-camera-worklets` is NOT installed, so `useFrameOutput`, `useAsyncRunner`, and passing a Reanimated SharedValue as `zoom`/`exposure` would throw, and must be avoided (reanimated is only a type import in the camera package).

gotchas: v4 APIs are gone: no `camera.current.takePhoto()`, no `photo={true}` / `video` / `format` / `useCameraFormat` / `pixelFormat` props, no static `Camera.requestCameraPermission()`. Capture lives on the output object (`photoOutput.capturePhoto`), not on the Camera ref. CameraRef only has focusTo/resetFocus/takeSnapshot/zoom-animation/controller/preview (src\views\Camera.tsx).
`capturePhoto(settings, callbacks)` and `capturePhotoToFile(settings, callbacks)` take TWO required positional args; pass `{}` for callbacks (src\specs\outputs\CameraPhotoOutput.nitro.ts).

All returned paths (`Photo.saveToTemporaryFileAsync()`, `PhotoFile.filePath`, `Image.saveToTemporaryFileAsync()`) are plain filesystem paths WITHOUT `file://`. RN `<Image source={{uri}}>` and fetch/upload need `'file://' + path`. Conversely `saveToFileAsync(path)` / `Images.loadFromFile(path)` must NOT get a `file://` prefix.

Temp files go to File.createTempFile('VisionCamera_', '.jpg') i.e. the app cache dir; nothing deletes them. expo-file-system is NOT a direct dependency (only nested at node_modules\expo\node_modules\expo-file-system), so there is no verified JS API in the project to delete/move them without adding a dependency.

`usePhotoOutput` memoizes on its option VALUES by reference: an inline `targetResolution={{width:..,height:..}}` creates a new CameraPhotoOutput every render, which changes `outputs` and forces a full session reconfigure each render. Use a `CommonResolutions.*` constant or a module-level/useMemo'd Size. An inline `outputs={[photoOutput]}` array is fine (useMemoizedArray flattens it).

Default photo target is UHD_4_3 (3024x4032). `photo.toImage()` decodes the whole JPEG to an ARGB_8888 Bitmap (~48 MB at 12MP) and may allocate a second rotated copy. For a 224x224 classifier request HD_4_3 / FHD_4_3. targetResolution is only a target; the actual size is `photoOutput.currentResolution` / `photo.width|height`.
`Image.resize(w,h)` stretches to exactly w x h (Bitmap.scale, no aspect preservation) - center-crop to a square first. `crop` takes (startX, startY, endX, endY), not (x, y, width, height).

`toRawPixelData()` returns 4 bytes/pixel; on Android the format is 'RGBA' (memory layout of ARGB_8888), on iOS typically 'BGRA'. Always branch on `raw.pixelFormat`; the model needs the alpha byte stripped to get [224,224,3].

Do NOT build the tensor via capturePhotoToFile -> Images.loadFromFile: Android's loadFromFile is BitmapFactory.decodeFile with no EXIF handling, and CameraX stores rotation in EXIF, so a portrait photo decodes sideways. `photo.toImageAsync()` applies rotation/mirroring physically - use that path.
`Photo.getPixelBuffer()` on a JPEG capture exposes the encoded JPEG plane, not RGB pixels; `hasPixelBuffer` being true does not mean decoded pixels.

Memory: Photo wraps a CameraX ImageProxy; you MUST call `photo.dispose()` (it calls image.close()). Undisposed photos can stall subsequent captures because CameraX limits outstanding images. Also dispose intermediate nitro Images (dispose() recycles the Bitmap) - but do not dispose an Image that is still being shown in a <NitroImage>.
`quality` scales differ: PhotoOutputOptions.quality is 0.0-1.0 (validated natively with require), nitro-image save/encode quality is 0-100.

`containerFormat: 'heic'` throws on Android ('PhotoContainerFormat "heic" is not supported on this Device!'); 'native' resolves to JPEG on Android. `qualityPrioritization: 'speed'` maps to ZERO_SHUTTER_LAG and errors if `device.supportsSpeedQualityPrioritization` is false. `flashMode: 'on'` throws if `device.hasFlash` is false.
`enableShutterSound` defaults to TRUE and the native side ORs it with CameraInfo.mustPlayShutterSound(), so some regions will always play it even when set to false.

Calling capturePhoto before the session is configured throws 'Photo Output is not yet attached to the CameraSession!'. Gate the shutter on the `onStarted` / `onPreviewStarted` callback (or catch and ignore).

Lifecycle: `isActive` only toggles session.start()/stop(). Android's CustomLifecycle already pauses on host Activity pause/resume, so AppState handling is not required, but navigation focus is NOT known to the library - drive `isActive` from `useIsFocused()` (expo-router re-exports it). Unmount stops and un-configures the session automatically; note the JS hook never calls session.dispose().

Default preview `implementationMode='performance'` uses a SurfaceView which per the docs 'does not support transparency or view layering'; if overlays, rounded corners or screen transitions misbehave, switch to implementationMode='compatible' (TextureView).

Worklets/frame processors: `react-native-vision-camera-worklets` is not installed, so `useFrameOutput`, `useAsyncRunner`, and passing a Reanimated SharedValue to `zoom`/`exposure` will throw at runtime. Keep zoom/exposure as plain numbers. Still capture needs none of reanimated/worklets.

No Expo config plugin ships with 5.2.3 (no app.plugin.js / plugin dir; package root contains only README.md, VisionCamera.podspec, android, ios, lib, nitro.json, nitrogen, package.json, react-native.config.js, src). The library's AndroidManifest declares only `<uses-feature camera/microphone required=false>` - the CAMERA permission must come from the app. It already does: C:\dk\mobile\app.json android.permissions includes android.permission.CAMERA and C:\dk\mobile\android\app\src\main\AndroidManifest.xml line 4 has it, so no native rebuild is needed for permissions. Do NOT add 'react-native-vision-camera' to app.json plugins - it would fail to resolve.

Library minSdk is 23 and compileSdk 36 (android\gradle.properties). Metro resolves the package via the 'react-native': 'src/index' field, TypeScript via lib/index.d.ts - both are present and export the same names.

The `CameraDevices.ts` helpers (getAllCameraDevices, getDefaultCameraDevice, addOnCameraDevicesChangedListener) are marked @deprecated in favour of hooks; importing the package index eagerly calls VisionCamera.createDeviceFactory() as a module side effect.

readers.summary: react-native-fast-tflite 3.0.1 is a Nitro module with a very small public surface: `loadTensorflowModel(source, delegates)` and `useTensorflowModel(source, delegates)` (both take a REQUIRED delegates array; `[]` = CPU), returning a `TfliteModel` HybridObject with `inputs`, `outputs`, `delegates`, `runSync(ArrayBuffer[]): ArrayBuffer[]` and `run(ArrayBuffer[]): Promise<ArrayBuffer[]>`. Inputs/outputs are raw `ArrayBuffer`s (NOT TypedArrays - Nitro throws in debug if you pass a Uint8Array; pass `.buffer`), and tensor metadata exposes only `{ name, dataType, shape }`. There is NO quantization metadata (no scale / zero_point) anywhere in the JS API and no dequantization: a uint8 model returns raw 0-255 bytes via memcpy, so we must branch on `model.outputs[0].dataType` ourselves and divide by 255 (approximation) for uint8. No worklet is required: the model is an ordinary JSI NativeState object usable from plain JS on the main RN runtime, can be held in a module-level singleton for the app's life, and `run()` executes inference on Nitro's C++ thread pool while `runSync()` blocks the calling JS thread. Two real hazards found in source: (a) output ArrayBuffers are cached per tensor name and REUSED across calls, so results must be copied before the next run; (b) the Android asset loader is just `java.net.URL(path).readBytes()`, which works with Metro's http URL in the dev build but will throw for `require()`'d assets in a release build where React Native resolves to a scheme-less resource identifier. Recommended: module-level `loadTensorflowModel(require('...tflite'), [])` promise singleton, build the input as a fresh exact-size Uint8Array/Float32Array chosen from `inputs[0].dataType`, call `await model.run([typed.buffer])`, immediately copy the output into a JS array, and serialize calls.

The native side copies `buffer->size()` bytes of the WHOLE ArrayBuffer; a TypedArray view's byteOffset/byteLength are ignored. If your RGB Uint8Array is a view into a larger buffer (common for data returned by native image libs), copy it into a fresh exactly-sized array first (or `.buffer.slice(byteOffset, byteOffset+byteLength)` as the README does at lines 139-144).

SILENT FAILURE on wrong input size: copyInputBuffers calls `TfLiteTensorCopyFromBuffer(tensor, buffer->data(), buffer->size())` and IGNORES the returned TfLiteStatus (cpp/HybridTfliteModel.cpp:98). The C API header states 'REQUIRES: input_data_size == TfLiteTensorByteSize(tensor)' (android/src/main/cpp/lib/litert/headers/tflite/core/c/c_api.h:638-641). A wrong-length buffer therefore does not throw - the model just runs on stale/zero input and returns plausible-looking garbage. Validate byteLength === product(shape) * bytesPerElement yourself before calling run.

OUTPUT BUFFERS ARE REUSED: getOutputBufferForTensor caches one native ArrayBuffer per output tensor name in `_outputBuffers` and copyOutputBuffers memcpy's into that same buffer on every call (cpp/HybridTfliteModel.cpp:102-137). The ArrayBuffer you got from a previous run() is overwritten by the next run(). Copy scores into a plain JS array immediately (Array.from / .slice()) before running again or storing in state.

NO DEQUANTIZATION and NO quantization metadata. Search of src/, cpp/, nitrogen/ and lib/typescript for quantiz|scale|zero_point finds nothing; the underlying C API has TfLiteTensorQuantizationParams (c_api.h:631-636) but the library never calls it. A uint8-quantized MobileNet returns raw bytes 0-255: read with `new Uint8Array(outputs[0])`. For ImageNet MobileNet-quant the output scale is ~1/256 with zero_point 0, so `v / 255` is a fine approximation for ranking/top-k; exact probabilities would require hardcoding scale/zero_point per model (read them in Netron). Ranking is unaffected either way because dequantization is monotonic.

Same for INPUT: a uint8 model wants raw 0-255 RGB bytes (1 byte/channel, 150528 bytes for 224x224x3); a float32 model wants 4 bytes/channel (602112 bytes) and YOU must normalize. The normalization ([-1,1] via (x-127.5)/127.5 for classic MobileNet v1/v2 float, vs [0,1] for some others) is not discoverable from the API - it is a property of the chosen model and must be recorded alongside it.

RELEASE-BUILD HAZARD on Android for `require('x.tflite')`: loadTensorflowModel uses `Image.resolveAssetSource(source).uri`. In the dev build that is Metro's `http://host:8081/assets/...` URL, which `java.net.URL(path).readBytes()` (HybridAssetLoader.kt) handles. In a release/embedded bundle React Native's AssetSourceResolver.defaultAsset() returns `resourceIdentifierWithoutScale()` on Android (C:\dk\mobile\node_modules\react-native\Libraries\Image\AssetSourceResolver.js:113-128) - a scheme-less resource name - and java.net.URL will throw MalformedURLException (no protocol). v3.0.1 has no resource-id fallback. Works today in the dev client; must be solved before a release APK (e.g. copy the asset to a file and pass `{ url: 'file://...' }`).

The dev-build model load goes over HTTP from Metro every cold start (the asset is fetched, then `ArrayBuffer.copy(bytes)`), so first load needs the Metro server reachable and a ~4-16 MB download; expect a noticeable first-load delay on device over Wi-Fi.

`tfliteModule.createModel` is a SYNCHRONOUS native call made on the JS thread after the async asset read (TfLiteModelCreate + TfLiteInterpreterCreate + AllocateTensors in the HybridTfliteModel constructor). The await in loadTensorflowModel does not make that part non-blocking; do the load at app start / screen mount, not on shutter press.

`runSync` blocks whatever thread calls it. From plain JS that is the RN JS thread (UI callbacks, navigation and touch handling on the JS side freeze for the inference duration, typically tens of ms for MobileNet on CPU but much longer on low-end devices in a debug build). Prefer `await model.run([...])`, which memcpy's input on the JS thread and runs TfLiteInterpreterInvoke on Nitro's ThreadPool (nitro-modules cpp/core/Promise.hpp:52-68).

No mutex protects the interpreter. `run()` dispatches to a multi-thread pool, so two in-flight run() calls (double-tap on the shutter) would write the input tensor and invoke concurrently on the same TfLiteInterpreter. Serialize calls in JS (promise chain or a busy flag).

No worklet is required anywhere. TfliteModel is a Nitro HybridObject backed by jsi::NativeState on the main RN runtime; its prototype methods are directly callable from ordinary JS. `NitroModules.box(model)` / `.unbox()` exists (nitro-modules src/NitroModulesProxy.ts:73) but the README (lines 110-114) says it is only needed for VisionCamera v4's worklet runtime. Since we classify a still photo, skip worklets and frame processors entirely.

Model lifetime: the HybridObject lives as long as a JS reference exists; GC triggers ~HybridTfliteModel which calls TfLiteInterpreterDelete. A module-level variable keeps it alive for the whole app session. `model.dispose()` exists on every HybridObject for eager release but the docs say it is optional ('use with caution') and the object is unusable afterwards. Fast Refresh re-evaluating the module will create a second interpreter in dev; harmless but uses memory until GC.

useTensorflowModel creates a NEW interpreter per hook instance and again whenever `source` changes; there is no internal cache. If the camera screen mounts/unmounts repeatedly the model is reloaded each time. Use the singleton and, if a hook is wanted, wrap the singleton promise.

`model.inputs` / `model.outputs` / `model.delegates` are native getters that rebuild a fresh array of structs on each property access (HybridTfliteModel.cpp:43-85). Read once after load and cache the Tensor objects.

readers.summary: Raw pixel access DOES exist in react-native-nitro-image 0.15.2, so no JPEG decoder or extra native dependency is needed. vision-camera 5.2.3 peer-depends on nitro-image and its Photo object has toImage()/toImageAsync() returning a nitro-image `Image` with orientation + mirroring already baked into the bitmap (HybridPhoto.kt lines 151-176); Image then offers crop/resize (sync and *Async variants, each returning a NEW Image), toRawPixelData()/toRawPixelDataAsync() returning { buffer: ArrayBuffer, width, height, pixelFormat }, and saveToTemporaryFileAsync(format, quality) returning a bare filesystem path (no file:// prefix). On Android the pixel data is a raw copyPixelsToBuffer() copy of an ARGB_8888 Bitmap, reported as pixelFormat 'RGBA' (bytes [R,G,B,A], 4 bytes/pixel, tightly packed, premultiplied alpha which is a no-op for opaque JPEG photos); on iOS it is typically 'BGRA', so code must branch on pixelFormat and drop the 4th byte to build the RGB tensor. Recommended path: photoOutput.capturePhoto() -> photo.saveToTemporaryFileAsync() (original JPEG with EXIF, for RN <Image> + upload) and photo.toImageAsync() -> cropAsync center square -> resizeAsync(224,224) -> toRawPixelData() -> strip alpha into Uint8Array/Float32Array -> model.run([typed.buffer]); dispose Photo and all Images in a finally block AFTER reading pixels. Avoid capturePhotoToFile + Images.loadFromFile for classification: BitmapFactory.decodeFile does not apply EXIF rotation, so the tensor would be sideways. Not installed: expo-image-manipulator, expo-image, jpeg-js, vision-camera-resize-plugin, react-native-nitro-web-image (expo-file-system and expo-asset exist only nested under node_modules/expo/node_modules); none are needed.

Never dispose an Image while <NitroImage>/<NativeNitroImage> is showing it: the Android view uses setImageBitmap(image.bitmap) on the same Bitmap and dispose() calls bitmap.recycle().

Prepend 'file://' for React Native <Image source={{uri}}> and fetch(). Temp files live in the app cache dir (File.createTempFile) and are never cleaned up automatically by either library.
Quality scales differ: vision-camera PhotoOutputOptions.quality is 0.0..1.0; nitro-image save/encode quality is 0..100 (throws outside that range, default 100).
Image.saveTo*('heic') throws on Android. Photo.saveToFileAsync/getFileData only support JPEG on Android (throws for other ImageFormats).
capturePhoto(settings, callbacks) requires BOTH arguments - pass {} for callbacks. enableShutterSound defaults to true.
loadImage/useImage/NitroImage with a { url } source throws at runtime because react-native-nitro-web-image is not installed; use { filePath } (file:// prefixes are stripped by normalizeFilePath).

react-native-fast-tflite 3.0.1 run()/runSync() take ArrayBuffer[] (not TypedArray[]) and return ArrayBuffer[]; loadTensorflowModel's delegates argument is mandatory. Make sure the TypedArray spans its whole buffer before passing .buffer.

react-native-nitro-image package.json lists app.plugin.js in `files`, but no app.plugin.js exists in the installed package - there is no Expo config plugin to add to app.json (autolinking via nitro.json is sufficient and it is already compiled).
README inaccuracies in the installed nitro-image: it writes `await image.toRawPixelData()` (it is sync) and `const image = useImage(...)` (the hook returns { image, error }).

CameraX's ImageProxy.toBitmap() is what HybridPhoto.toImage() relies on for JPEG decoding; its behaviour for JPEG_ULTRA_HDR output (if photoHDR gets enabled in the session config) was not inspected - keep HDR off / containerFormat 'jpeg'.

Upload payload: upload the original full-resolution JPEG from photo.saveToTemporaryFileAsync(), or a downsized copy via image.resize(...).saveToTemporaryFileAsync('jpg', 80) (no EXIF, already upright)? Not decided by this investigation.

# 3) (later) Embedding model: MobileNetV3-Small feature vector, output [1,1024], 1.tflite = 6,105,072 bytes

# ---- FALLBACK (static GCS URL, uint8, labels included, 3,069,250-byte zip) ----
# curl -L --fail -o m.zip "https://storage.googleapis.com/download.tensorflow.org/models/tflite/mobilenet_v1_1.0_224_quant_and_labels.zip"
# unzip -j m.zip mobilenet_v1_1.0_224_quant.tflite labels_mobilenet_quant_v1_224.txt -d assets/models && rm m.zip

// ---- TypeScript (uses only APIs verified in react-native-fast-tflite 3.0.1 sources) ----
import { loadTensorflowModel, type TfliteModel } from 'react-native-fast-tflite'
import labels from '../assets/models/imagenet_labels.json' // string[1001], [0] = 'background'

let model: TfliteModel | undefined
export async function getClassifier(): Promise<TfliteModel> {
  if (model) return model
  model = await loadTensorflowModel(require('../assets/models/mobilenet_v3_small_224_cls.tflite'), [])
  const i = model.inputs[0], o = model.outputs[0]
  // Expected: float32 [1,224,224,3] in and float32 [1,1001] out. Fail loudly, because a
  // wrong-size input is silently ignored by the native side.
  if (i.dataType !== 'float32' || i.shape.join() !== '1,224,224,3' || o.shape[o.shape.length - 1] !== 1001)
    throw new Error(`Unexpected model IO: ${JSON.stringify({ i, o })}`)
  return model
}

/** rgb: 224*224*3 bytes, RGB order, 0..255 (from whatever resize/pixel-read step is used) */
export async function classify(rgb: Uint8Array, topK = 5) {
  const m = await getClassifier()
  const input = new Float32Array(224 * 224 * 3)
  for (let p = 0; p < input.length; p++) input[p] = rgb[p] / 255 // [0,1], NOT [-1,1]
  const [out] = await m.run([input.buffer as ArrayBuffer])
  const logits = new Float32Array(out.slice(0)) // copy, because the output buffer is reused natively
  let max = -Infinity; for (const v of logits) if (v > max) max = v
  let sum = 0; const probs = new Float32Array(logits.length)
  for (let k = 0; k < logits.length; k++) { probs[k] = Math.exp(logits[k] - max); sum += probs[k] }
  return Array.from(probs, (v, k) => ({ index: k, label: labels[k], score: v / sum }))
    .filter(r => r.index !== 0) // drop 'background'
    .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score).slice(0, topK)
}

fast-tflite caches and reuses output ArrayBuffers per tensor name (HybridTfliteModel.cpp:103-113), so the ArrayBuffer returned by run() is overwritten by the next run(). Copy it (`out.slice(0)`) before storing or sorting results.

A 10.2 MB float model bundled through Metro is served over http in dev, so the first load is a 10 MB transfer from the dev machine to the phone. It works, but expect a second or two of delay. If APK size matters, the uint8 fallback is 4.3 MB (V1) or 3.6 MB (V2) and needs neither normalisation nor softmax, at the cost of a different input dtype: pass the Uint8Array buffer directly, 150,528 bytes.
open_questions: The actual tensor dtypes, shapes and quantisation parameters of every candidate were taken from model cards, not from the flatbuffers, because downloads were prohibited. After fetching, log model.inputs and model.outputs once. For the recommended model I expect input float32 [1,224,224,3] and output float32 [1,1001].

fast-tflite's Tensor type does not expose quantisation scale or zero-point (Tflite.nitro.ts:31-35 has only name, dataType and shape). If the uint8 fallback is used, the output dequantisation (conventionally prob = byte/256 or byte/255) has to be assumed or checked in Netron. For top-K ranking it does not matter, since raw bytes sort the same way.

The release-build asset resolution for require()'d .tflite files on Android was inferred from HybridAssetLoader.kt (`URL(path).readBytes()`) and was not exercised. It needs a test in a release variant, or the loader should be designed around a file:// URL from the start.

How long will the mobilenet_v3 and mobilenet_v2 GCS buckets stay at 403? The result was the same for small, large and the v2 float checkpoints, which suggests the buckets were locked down rather than a transient error, but I could not confirm the cause.

How long will the anonymous Kaggle download endpoint remain stable? It worked without credentials today (302 then 206). If the project wants zero dependency on it, commit the extracted .tflite files to the repo (Apache-2.0 permits redistribution; keep a NOTICE or attribution line) rather than fetching them at build time.

ImageNet-1k classes are a poor semantic match for a worker-marketplace problem picker. The labels include generic objects such as 'plunger', 'power drill', 'washbasin', 'toilet seat', 'space heater', 'switch' and 'screwdriver', but not faults such as 'leaking pipe'. A mapping table from ImageNet labels to DikhaDo categories, or the 1024-d feature-vector model plus a small nearest-centroid or linear head, is probably the real day-two path. This is outside the sourcing concern, but it affects whether the classifier or the embedder should ship first.

No babel.config.js is needed. With no Babel config file in C:\dk\mobile (there is none), Expo's Metro transformer falls back to `require('expo/internal/babel-preset')`, which is babel-preset-expo 57.0.12. That preset pushes `react-native-worklets/plugin` automatically when it resolves from the project root, and it does (checked with require.resolve). Installed versions are reanimated 4.5.1 and worklets 0.10.1, the exact pins in expo/bundledNativeModules.json, and reanimated's compatibility.json lists 4.5.x with RN 0.86 and worklets 0.10.x.

Reanimated still exports `runOnJS`, but only as a @deprecated alias of the worklets one. The replacement is `scheduleOnRN(fn, ...args)` from 'react-native-worklets'; it takes the args inline instead of returning a function. `useSharedValue`, `useAnimatedStyle`, `withTiming`, `withSpring`, `withDelay`, `withSequence`, `Easing`, `interpolate`, `ReduceMotion`, `useReducedMotion` and `ReducedMotionConfig` all exist with the signatures listed below. The default export is the `Animated` namespace (`Animated.View`, `Animated.Image`).

For reduce motion, Reanimated's `useReducedMotion()` returns a constant read once at app start. Every withTiming/withSpring already defaults to `ReduceMotion.System`: the value jumps to `toValue` and the completion callback still fires with `finished === true`, so the choreography needs no branching. RN 0.86's `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled(): Promise<boolean>` and the 'reduceMotionChanged' event also exist if a live value is wanted.

expo-router 57.0.22 vendors React Navigation inside its own build, and `@react-navigation/*` is not installed at all. `useIsFocused`, `useFocusEffect`, `useNavigation` and `Stack` must be imported from 'expo-router'. The root layout already sets `screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }}`, so a full-screen camera route needs nothing extra.
